snip.t: Autoimmune: Autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis
Cirrhosis (alcoholic, viral, autoimmune), schistosomiasis, congenital hepatic fibrosis, primary biliary cholangitis, sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (veno-occlusive disease), and sarcoidosis.

Aetiology: chronic alcohol use, chronic viral hepatitis (B, C), non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, autoimmune hepatitis, biliary disease (primary biliary cholangitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis), haemochromatosis, Wilson disease, alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency.
Seen in gallstones, biliary obstruction and primary biliary cholangitis.
Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) — bile duct destruction; AMA (anti-mitochondrial antibody) positive; causes pruritus

qs.q: Which autoantibody is classically positive in Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC), a condition involving bile duct destruction and pruritus?
qs.e: Primary Biliary Cholangitis is characterized by bile duct destruction and is positive for anti-mitochondrial antibodies (AMA). Antinuclear and smooth muscle antibodies are typically seen in autoimmune hepatitis.
qs.s: Clinical Chemical Pathology Crash Course — Part 2: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following serum autoantibodies is found in over 95% of patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC)?
qs.e: Anti-mitochondrial antibody (AMA) is found in over 95% of patients with PBC. SMA is typically associated with autoimmune hepatitis.
